task.title: Checking What References the Changed Content
task.shortdesc: Before you change a reused element, a topic or a key, use the References tab to list the maps and topics that the change affects.

keywords.indexterm: References tabchecking the effect of a change

prereq.p: Turn on the tab: open your Profile page and, in the Preferences section, select Show the DITA References tab in the Explore side view.

step.cmd: Open the file that holds the content in the editor, and place the caret inside the element that you want to change.
step.info: For example, place it inside a warning that other topics reuse by content reference.

step.stepresult: The Explore side view opens on the References tab and shows the file in the Referenced by direction. If other files reference elements of the file, the tab groups them by element, and it highlights the group of the element at the caret.

step.cmd: Read the files under the highlighted Element id group.
step.info: Each file in the group references the element. A number next to a file shows how many times the file references it.

step.cmd: To follow the references further, expand a file.
step.info: The file opens on the files that reference it in turn. For example, a topic opens on the maps that include it, and a map opens on the maps that include it, up to the root map of each publication.

step.cmd: To see only what one publication includes, choose it as the context publication and click Use the context publication as scope on the toolbar.
step.info: The tab then applies the publication's profiling and resolves keys as the publication does. See .

step.cmd: Click a file to open the referencing file in the editor, at the element that holds the reference.

result.p: You have the list of the files to check, or to update, after you make the change.

example.title: Example: What Does a Map Pull In?
example.p: To learn what a map includes, open it in the editor and click the References tab icon in the Explore side view. The tab starts on the root map of the active publication. To show another map, type part of its name in the field at the top of the tab. Then click References. The tab lists the topics, the keys, the maps and the images that the map references, and each file opens on what it references in turn.
